summary: Stephan Licha is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Japanology who earned his PhD from SOAS University of London in 2012. He completed postdoctoral work at Waseda University and the University of Tokyo, and joined the University of Chicago faculty (attested 2026).
Stephan Marcus Salzberg is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of British Columbia (attested 1983) under Yoshitaka Iriya, Shoko Kanaoka, and Daniel L. Overmyer.

Stephan V. Beyer (born 1943) works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Rochester and under Richard Hugh Robinson (~1967–1970). He served as a professor at the University of Wisconsin–Madison (~1971–1979) and held a post at Sidley Austin.

Stephanie Kaza works in religious and Buddhist studies. She studied at Oberlin, Stanford, UC Santa Cruz, and Starr King School for the Ministry, learning under Thich Nhat Hanh and Joanna Macy. She taught at the University of Vermont (1991; Professor Emeritus 2005–2015).
Stephanie Roemer is a scholar of Tibetology who completed her doctoral studies under supervisors Eberhard Sandschneider and Toni Huber.

Stephanie W. Jamison (born 1948) is an Indologist and linguist. She completed her doctorate at Yale (~1972–1977) under Stanley Insler and Warren Crawford Cowgill. She held posts at Harvard (~1986–2002) and became Professor of Sanskrit and Indo-Iranian Linguistics at UCLA in ~2002.

Stephen Addiss (1935–2022) specialized in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and art history. He earned degrees from Harvard and the University of Michigan (1971–1977). He was professor of art history at the University of Kansas (1977–1992) and held an endowed professorship at the University of Richmond (1992–2013).

Stephen Batchelor (born 1953) is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar. He studied under teachers including Geshe Rabten, Kusan Sunim, and Richard Gombrich. He directed Sharpham College (~1996–2000), which he founded in 1996, and became core faculty at Bodhi College (~2015).

Stephen C. Berkwitz works in Buddhist and religious studies. He held a Fulbright fellowship at the University of Kelaniya (1995–1997). His career includes posts at Missouri State University (attested 2004, 2013) and a visiting research fellowship at Ruhr University Bochum.

Stephen F. Teiser (born 1956) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religion. He studied at Oberlin and Princeton (Master's and PhD ~1980–1986) under Denis Twitchett, Alan Sponberg, and Daniel L. Overmyer. He joined Princeton's faculty in ~1988, becoming D. T. Suzuki Professor in ~1996.

Stephen Fuchs (1908–2000) was an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He studied under Wilhelm Schmidt and earned a PhD from the University of Vienna (~1948–1950). He founded the Anthropos Institute (1950) and lectured at St. Xavier's College, Mumbai (1950–1954).

Stephen G. Covell (born 1965) is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He completed his doctoral studies at Princeton University (~1995–2001) under Jacqueline I. Stone and held a post at Western Michigan University from ~2003.
Stephen H. Phillips works in philosophy and Indology. He served as a professor of philosophy at the University of Texas at Austin (attested 1999) and is attested there as professor emeritus in 2026.

Stephen Harris is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD from the University of New Mexico in 2014 and serves as a University Lecturer in Indian and Comparative Philosophy at Leiden University (attested 2026).

Stephen J. Laumakis is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who studied under John Kronen, Ramdas Lamb, George J. Tanabe, and David West. He served as Associate Professor of Philosophy at the University of St. Thomas (attested 2008–2013).

Stephen Jenkins is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Harvard under doctoral supervisors Masatoshi Nagatomi and Charles Hallisey, among other teachers. He served as Professor of Religious Studies at California State Polytechnic University, Humboldt (attested 2010–2013).

Stephen Prothero (born 1960) is a religious studies scholar. He earned degrees at Yale and Harvard (PhD ~1986–1990) under William R. Hutchison. In ~1996, he joined Boston University, where he became C. Allyn and Elizabeth V. Russell Professor Emeritus of Religion in America.

Stephen R. Bokenkamp (born 1949) is a Sinologist and religious studies scholar who studied at UC Berkeley (~1978–1986). He taught Classical Chinese at Indiana University Bloomington (~1989–2007) and became Professor of Chinese at Arizona State University in ~2007.
Stephen Suen is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed his PhD at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2009) under the doctoral supervision of K. L. Dhammajoti.

Stephen Wootton Bushell (1844–1908) was a Sinologist and archaeologist. He studied at Guy's Hospital Medical School and the University of London (MD ~1866–1868). He served as house surgeon at Guy's Hospital (1866) and resident medical officer at Bethlem Royal Hospital (1867).
